svg.title: Perseverance's seven minutes of terror
svg.desc: Animated timeline of Perseverance's entry, descent and landing (EDL) on 18 February 2021, from site/data/mars2020-edl.json. Top track: spacecraft time after entry interface (E+): entry at 5.32 km/s (≈128 km up), peak heating ≈E+75 s (≈1,300 °C press kit) and peak deceleration 10.7 g at E+83 s, parachute at E+241 s (433 m/s, Mach 1.76, 12.2 km), heat shield separation E+263 s (158 m/s), backshell separation and powered descent E+358 s (81 m/s, 2.1–2.2 km), sky crane E+407 s (constant 0.75 m/s from ≈20 m), touchdown E+419 s at 0.77 m/s vertical. A glyph above the track changes with each phase. Bottom track: Earth receives each event one-way light time later, 682 s = 11 min 22 s (press kit), shown as radio pulses that all take the same time to fall from one track to the other; Earth hears 'entry' 263 s after the rover has already landed. Time is compressed 70×.
svg.text: times after entry (E+), as seen on each world

g.text: Radio waves need 11 min 22 s to cross 204 million km to Earth.
Perseverance is already down, but Earth has not even heard it hit the air.
Earth watches all seven minutes, 11 min 22 s late. Nobody could help.
